Our Space
---------------
Our space is hard to describe but we have been compared to a scrappy McMenamin's We have a large space but very clean and magical ( built as a hotel in 1904) our historical building has been lovingly restored .
We are not your usual space so please read carefully... think old school hotel / European hostel without the ghosts....or maybe there are ghosts you will have to see (wink wink) No ghosts that  are too precocious I promise :)
We have three shared and very clean bathrooms
One very well stocked kitchen (pots, pans, dishes and the like provided)

I LOVE LOVE LOVE being a host, traveling and meeting awesome people. I have recently adopted a little girl doggie named Pickles who is sweet and learning how to greet people, she came all the way from Mexico but is not traumatized at all, if you are allergic to dogs then please let me know before hand so i can have her in my office.

   I  easy going person and  always try to keep our space filled with good energy. We welcome all respectful people here, this is a safe space.

host_about:
Airbnb, it seems, is changing, but I'm not.  In a time when the prevailing model seems to be anonymous key drops and hosts you never meet I shall continue to be a relic, making sure to greet you personally if at all possible, tell you a bit about the neighborhood, and just  generally make a human connection.  I've been doing this 10 years or so now and I feel like I've got a pretty good handle on how to be a good host.  I build, furnish, and clean both my units myself so I know exactly what you'll see when you arrive and I know that it will be done right.  I build spaces that I would want to (and frequently do) hang out in myself.  My units are unique, comfortable, and well located just a couple of blocks from the centre of one of the best neighborhoods to visit in Seattle.
So, if you're looking for an anonymous experience where you let yourself into someone's IKEA furnished basement that you can bring home hookers to with no one noticing or caring you might want to consider one of the many other offerings on Airbnb that will better cater to your needs...  This is not to say I will be a constant presence during your stay.  I generally welcome my guests and then leave them alone to enjoy their visit.  Some folks are more gregarious and I've also made many new friends over the past decade whom I enjoy staying in touch with.  That's really entirely up to you.
I will ask one, to me, very important thing of you as a guest, which is to communicate your arrival plans to me and to respond in a timely fashion when I ask about them.  I will send you carefully timed texts messages with things like directions, parking tips should you have a car, and so on.  I will go out of my way to get you in early if that is what you need and if it is at all possible.  I will store your bags for the day if you're checking out and want to enjoy your day without dragging them around.  I will offer suggestions and be available by text most of each day to help you out and make sure you have the best visit possible  But I'm not a trained monkey in a pill box hat sitting at the concierge desk all day waiting around on your mysterious arrival time.  I have a life, of sorts, and I arrange it around your schedule so that your travel days are smooth.  
I will probably ask you for you flight info if that's how you're coming in.  It's really not a big mystery and is super helpful to me in tracking early/late arrivals so I can be sure to be here when you arrive while also scheduling my "life".
I very much enjoy hosting.  I like meeting my guests and sharing my knowledge of my city with them.  This is not something I do because I screwed up and got in over my head on a bad mortgage.  Yes, I make part of my living this way.  No, I don't really need to.  My motivation is the hundreds of great reviews that you see here that are a reflection of all the wonderful people I've been lucky enough to meet and to pass a short time with over the years.  I would like you to be one of them.  People invariably ask me about bad experiences I've had.  I honestly have trouble thinking of any.  A few moments have been challenging (I still haven't found all the glitter from that wedding...) but most people are great when you meet them and, in my experience, none have any malice in their hearts or intentions when they arrive.  Perhaps some hosts bring that out in folks.  I don't.  We're totally going to get along.  You'll see...

This classic beauty is decorated in simple calming colors for an enjoyable stay, A soothing space in the historic hotel offers an old world touch of charm. The room is furnished with memory foam mattress, antique desk and shelf for clothing.
Free Wi-Fi and parking . All linens, towels, soaps provided.
Need extra pillows or anything feel free to ask. We are here to make your stay go smoothly
neighborhood_overview:
Georgetown neighborhood is so much fun and it has a unique flare. This neighborhood is creative arts district . Please also read our reviews as it may not be a good fit for everyone.Its a slightly industrial area and gritty in interesting ways. It's very safe and usually lots of people on the street who are enjoying a myriad of restaurants, vintage stores, record stores and especially fun is The Georgetown Trailer Park Mall located in our parking lot on the weekends. We have lots of fun things to do including a circus school and glass blowing studios, high end design collectives all located within easy walking distance. Foodies love it here. You do not have to be creative to stay here, just open to different types of people and experiences.

Transportation
The number 124 Bus is right across the street and goes directly to down town and the light link rail. Georgetown is hoppin come see it for yourself and read our reviews. Industrial Arts district meets thriving comme
host_about:
I am a visual artist who is  the  director of a community  Arts Center, art studios and guest rooms co-mingle to create a fun experience if you choose. Original art lines the hallways and some of the rooms  of our space, which is a restored Hotel and we welcome all including non artists with open arms. Not Arty at all? that's ok we are also close to stadiums, downtown,  nature  (Kubota Gardens, the arboretum, Seward Park, Alki Beach, Lincoln Park, Schmitz Park,  and yep golfing options (West Seattle and Jefferson Park both have awesome courses). We are also located up the street from the Boeing Flight museum and school , Northwest Institute of Asian and Oriental medicine (NIAOM) and also   The School of Acrobatics and Circus arts (SANCA) and not far away from Fed Ex and Amazon downtown.

Are you a foodie ???
We have soooo many amazing restaurants in the area (South Park, Georgetown  Beacon hill and White Center ) of course down town also but if you want to spread the  love in the neighborhood then just look at my guide book (south Seattle's finest)  

Our Space
---------------
Our space is hard to describe but we have been compared to a scrappy McMenamin's We have a large space but very clean and magical ( built as a hotel in 1904) our historical building has been lovingly restored .
We are not your usual space so please read carefully... think old school hotel / European hostel without the ghosts....or maybe there are ghosts you will have to see (wink wink) No ghosts that  are too precocious I promise :)
We have three shared and very clean bathrooms
One very well stocked kitchen (pots, pans, dishes and the like provided) 
And if you enjoy a morning coffee or tea / or evening glass of wine (or smoke) we have a very expansive back porch with couches , tables and a designated smoking area (New Orleans meets Georgetown)

 If you are sick please do not travel.  I'm a fairly warm person, i like to give hugs but currently I am keeping social distancing and ask that if you visit us that you do also.  
About Me 
I LOVE LOVE LOVE being a host, traveling and meeting awesome people. I have recently adopted a little girl doggie named Pickles who is sweet and learning how to greet people, she came all the way from Mexico but is not traumatized at all, if you are allergic to dogs then please let me know before hand so i can have her in my office.   
 The building is truly a magical charmer and  I think you will enjoy your stay here

Special things to be aware of
* I follow Airbnb’s enhanced cleaning protocol, which was developed with expert guidance.


***Please note that the rooms are on the second floor and we unfortunately are not ADA accesible. 

***Also of note our space is in the city so it's active and not always cricket quiet some noise from events , street or airplanes may happen, if you need a super quiet space book a hotel in the country. Most of the time the building itself is quiet but we have planes that fly overhead and a hopping building with fun restaurants and a pool hall downstairs. 

HANDS ON / only one staff member / so please be communicative
 I only have one staff member and do all cleaning, booking and greeting (except evening arrivals) myself so it is appreciated that you let me know your arrival time (as close as possible) at the time of your booking request and communicate this when you book if possible. I greet you in person or our evening manager if your arrival is after 6 pm 
***After 10 pm arrivals \late arrivals will require a $20 hr surcharge**. Late arrivals  with prior arrangement may be accepted) please inform me of your arrival time at the time of your booking request. Of course we know that emergencies happen ( delayed flights are real) and will work with you to make sure you are safe and respected

About ME
   I am an artist , entrepreneur and lover of people, plants and four legged beings. Sadly we can not allow animals in the rooms at this time unless they are a documented service animal with a vets authorization (must provide before booking)
   I  easy going person and  always try to keep our space filled with good energy. We welcome all respectful people here, this is a safe space. 
* please be vaccinated so we may keep everyone safe. Currently we are not requiring masking or social distancing in shared spaces , but you may do what ever makes you comfortable and please if you are immunocompromised just let us know and we will also wear our masks for you. Just let us know.


WANT TO GET MARRIED WHILE YOUR HERE?
  Well we have a wedding chapel on our property called Shotgun ceremonies
 ( you can find online) if ya wanna get hitched while your here. :) 
The lovely officiant of Shotgun ceremonies can work with you on a wedding package ( and yes Elvis can be present ) believe it!!
( I am not  the officiant...so please do not ask me about setting up the details ) but if you book thru her then you can also organize your guests rooms with me,
If you organize  / coordinate  to rent ALL the rooms in our space (There are 8 room), I will give you a 10% off the total (one point of contact only please for simplicity)  
****Please no non Airbnb guests onsite unless they are helping you with your luggage , or help up and down stairs

****NO SMOKING of anything inside BUILDING / NO VAPING/
 …you can do all these things in our Smoking area outside. I  am easily accessible if you need anything, I am happy to oblige most requests and strive to make every traveler feel welcome  but I also will give you your space. I try to take Sundays off to rest and have time with my dog. (Dog lives off site )
I am also happy to  help you plan a fun day here in Seattle.  I have allot of travel info and happy to give you any recommendations . 


We look forward to meeting you and making your stay awesome!

To earn more about our community of Just search Georgetown Seattle
My life motto
"Life is short, art is long"

neighborhood_overview: Great walking neighborhood with many coffee, dining and pub locations to choose from right in the neighborhood. host_about:
My roots are in Alaska, with many family members still living and working up there. I love to hike, ski, mountain bike, kayak, dig in the dirt, eat good food, and travel.  My husband is a furniture designer  whose workshop is located in the "Center of the Universe" (Fremont!) and is now the designated grill master with his specialty; wild Alaskan Salmon caught by our son!  Our other son was instrumental in getting this apartment up and running. Both occasionally come by for a few days at a time. 

We also have a karelian bear dog  that is now older than me in dog years. She is sweet, mellow, and loves a hello. She lives outside during the days and when we are home joins us upstairs. She often takes doggy vacations with our son for a few days or longer that she absolutely loves.
  
I spend my winter months surrounded by sweet, loving 6, 7, and 8 year olds teaching them to read and love books! 

We're happy to share our knowledge of Seattle and surroundings. We can send you off on some great trips culled from our many years of exploring the Northwest!

How many ways do I love my neighborhood? Hard to count. It just gets better and better as does Seattle in general. I will post more here later but Fremont is a great area to choose for your visit - location, amenities, fun things to do, great shops and restaurants, live music venues
….
host_about:
I love art and "creation." I love to travel.  I look forward to winter snowshoeing, some US travel, hosting on airbnb and a trip to Germany (Autumn 2019).  2020 will be my 8th year as an airbnb host.   I speak French and Spanish (much better French) and I have worked in education, real estate, video, and parade art ensemble builds. 

My home is in the "center of the Universe" in the artsy and eclectic Fremont area - where you find the Troll under Aurora bridge, a great PCC coop, banks, shops, cafes, and a great night life as well.  

2020 Holiday Season
Holiday events in and around Fremont include the lighting of the Lenin Statue (for real), a parade of caroling boats creating truly heavenly sounds, the annual Winter Feast on or close to Dec 21, great shopping for unique gifts at all the local shops, First Friday art walk, New Years Eve spectacular fire works on Lake Union, and access to all the Seattle 2020 holiday excitement including the Nutcracker with the Pacific Northwest Ballet, and Seattle Symphony's New Years Eve Party!  

Summer Solstice
The famous Fremont Solstice Parade happens every June close to summer solstice.  Creator of the Ice Queenistas 2009-2012  I was an Ice Queen Clown in 2014  and accompanied a 7 foot articulated wolf/dog made from reed and white papier machee created by local artist, Sarah Lovett. In 2015 I was a banner carrier with the lead Samba ensemble group Girasol.  

The Neighborhood
As to the Fremont neighborhood, I moved here years ago thinking I'd stay a couple of years but many lattes, parades  and  3 homes later, I'm still here.  We have a smaller community of artsy, smart and creative people with heart, in the middle of the big city.  I live on a hill and have a great view of Mt Rainier on a sunny / clear day from one of the rooms and the back deck.  And it's always great to come home to this charming and awesome neighborhood.

FOODIE w/o gluten!!
After years, and maybe more years, I'm pretty much gluten and heavy carb free.  My cooking includes salads, chicken, veggies both raw and cooked, broths and soups, coffee, tea, coconut and chocolate desserts.  Love coconut oil and fresh salmon.
But I taste just about everything and never turn my nose up my guests regional cooking shares.

MORE...
For myself living without the open road, great friends, dream time, and my favorite shoes including some well seasoned ostrich boots from the Boot Lady in Seattle, is not an option.  

AND along with 2 treetop rooms upstairs, the cute and lovable 1 bedroom apartment is available for you too.  With a full kitchen and bath, and a great 40" Vizio flat screen that works with your chrome cast service,  you will love it. If you want extra privacy, your own fridge and cooking space,  and/or room for a couple of friends to travel with you, pick this option.  If you want 100% remodeled please continue your search.  If you love the unique and artistic life, clean, well supplied and situated on a country lane in the city do check out "Super cool in artsy Fremont"!     

Favorite coffee - Lighthouse Roaster from right up the street at 43rd and Phinney.
Favorite view - from the sun dial at the top of Gas Works Park hill.
Favorite Seattle park - Discovery Park
What I think about Eastern WA - it's an excellent secret - with wide open valleys, rolling hills, rivers, wheat fields and when the rain is over the top in Seattle, there's nearly always SUN!

How I feel about Puget Sound - big love - have to hop a ferry at least a few times a year to visit an Island or the Olympic Penninsula; have to walk on a gravel beach and skip a few rocks to remember the incomparable beauty of the place; seagulls make me happy.  Mt. Rainier is my sacred mountain - it calls me each year at least once to hike or snowshoe and feel the awesome presence of its magnetic core.  

I love traveling in France and Europe in general, Mexico, the American West and Southwest, and now, South America.  My favorite way to travel is to friends or family who live there.  Or with a group of like minded people on a small group tour.  Or by car locally and in the Southwest where the wide open spaces bring freedom to my soul.

neighborhood_overview: If you're coming here it's probably because you know about Fremont and want to stay here.  If you don't, it considers itself to the the "Center of the Universe" and was Seattle's historic artsy neighborhood.  It has since become home to a lot of high tech and has grown while still hanging onto it's roots. host_about:
Airbnb, it seems, is changing, but I'm not.  In a time when the prevailing model seems to be anonymous key drops and hosts you never meet I shall continue to be a relic, making sure to greet you personally if at all possible, tell you a bit about the neighborhood, and just  generally make a human connection.  I've been doing this 10 years or so now and I feel like I've got a pretty good handle on how to be a good host.  I build, furnish, and clean both my units myself so I know exactly what you'll see when you arrive and I know that it will be done right.  I build spaces that I would want to (and frequently do) hang out in myself.  My units are unique, comfortable, and well located just a couple of blocks from the centre of one of the best neighborhoods to visit in Seattle.
So, if you're looking for an anonymous experience where you let yourself into someone's IKEA furnished basement that you can bring home hookers to with no one noticing or caring you might want to consider one of the many other offerings on Airbnb that will better cater to your needs...  This is not to say I will be a constant presence during your stay.  I generally welcome my guests and then leave them alone to enjoy their visit.  Some folks are more gregarious and I've also made many new friends over the past decade whom I enjoy staying in touch with.  That's really entirely up to you.
I will ask one, to me, very important thing of you as a guest, which is to communicate your arrival plans to me and to respond in a timely fashion when I ask about them.  I will send you carefully timed texts messages with things like directions, parking tips should you have a car, and so on.  I will go out of my way to get you in early if that is what you need and if it is at all possible.  I will store your bags for the day if you're checking out and want to enjoy your day without dragging them around.  I will offer suggestions and be available by text most of each day to help you out and make sure you have the best visit possible  But I'm not a trained monkey in a pill box hat sitting at the concierge desk all day waiting around on your mysterious arrival time.  I have a life, of sorts, and I arrange it around your schedule so that your travel days are smooth.  
I will probably ask you for you flight info if that's how you're coming in.  It's really not a big mystery and is super helpful to me in tracking early/late arrivals so I can be sure to be here when you arrive while also scheduling my "life".
I very much enjoy hosting.  I like meeting my guests and sharing my knowledge of my city with them.  This is not something I do because I screwed up and got in over my head on a bad mortgage.  Yes, I make part of my living this way.  No, I don't really need to.  My motivation is the hundreds of great reviews that you see here that are a reflection of all the wonderful people I've been lucky enough to meet and to pass a short time with over the years.  I would like you to be one of them.  People invariably ask me about bad experiences I've had.  I honestly have trouble thinking of any.  A few moments have been challenging (I still haven't found all the glitter from that wedding...) but most people are great when you meet them and, in my experience, none have any malice in their hearts or intentions when they arrive.  Perhaps some hosts bring that out in folks.  I don't.  We're totally going to get along.  You'll see...

As a neighborhood, Queen Anne can refer either to the entire hill or to the central residential and business district at the top of the hill. Lower Queen Anne, refers to the area at the southern base of the hill, just north and west of Seattle Center.

The district’s name derives from the architectural style, typical of so many of the early houses in this area. The historic mansions are home to many of Seattle's economic and cultural elite.

Occasionally we will take the resort route but for the most part we prefer to stay in other people's homes for a home away from home experience. We've done home swaps with other families as well.

To spend time in a progressive, cultured city and still be able to experience such lush and beautiful outdoor recreation is a rare find. We love introducing people to Seattle and the surrounding areas and helping them to experience a little piece of our world.

There is even an organic chocolate factory in the neighborhood...offering tours and free samples!  There are a lot of local neighborhood art installations as well. host_about:
My favorite things are family, spirituality, natural healthy living, yoga, movies and meeting new people and experiencing new things.

I come from a large family, and I have a large family.  I love them all!  I am a sister to three brothers and two sisters.  I have five children along with their five spouses, who have blessed me with nine grand children.  I guess that means that I identify primarily as a mother and a grandmother.  

I love to learn about and put into practice natural and healthy food and dietary choices, sustainable living choices, natural healing methods, etc.  

I also love to watch movies, but not so much the big box movies as the smaller independent and foreign films.  I have quite a collection of them.

I attend yoga classes two or three times a week and find it a very rewarding system of exercise for my body.

I'm married to a wonderful man, Kirk Jolley.  We have been together for about 20 years.  He is a very talented builder and contractor.  He delights in making older homes beautiful again and he is very good at what he does.  

We often travel to Hawaii, since one son lives there with his family.  We also like to go to Mexico and Canada.  I like staying in homes, apartments or condos because I like having my own kitchen or kitchenette.  An unfortunate natural gas exposure has left me with extreme sensitivity to petroleum products, and consequently many scented products and foods.  This requires me to ask about heating and cooking fuels in homes, as well as cleaning products or strongly scented products used therein.

My father was a Scout Master and took us camping a lot.  He taught us to always leave a place cleaner than we found it.  I still do that!  My husband often tells me that I am doing the maids job when I clean up a place before I leave it, but I can't help it...it is ingrained in me.  My kids thought I was a bit of a neat freak, but I've noticed that they learned well, and they all know how to clean and they keep their homes tidy...even the boys.  Needless to say, I would take good care of anyone's place that I stayed in.

neighborhood_overview:
It's charming, historical, safe, beautiful views and a perfect location for seeing the best of what Seattle offers. I am seven blocks from a major shopping area; Trader Joes, Safeway, Bartell Drugs, dozens of bars and restaurants offering an array of cuisines. (lots of Happy Hours), as well as boutiques and shops. I am one block from a major viewpoint where everyone gathers to watch the 4th of July fireworks. and one block from the bus stop that takes you directly to Seattle Center, downtown, and Pike Place Market. These are the two areas with the the majority of attractions, exhibits, museums, shopping, and people watching. Seattle Center hosts the EMP (experience music project) owned by Paul Allen, the Chihuly glass museum, the Space Needle, Pacific Science Center, IMAX theater, and ongoing festivals.

The downtown area has many attractions, Pike Place Market, the waterfront, the Aquarium, Seattle Art Museum (SAM), boat cruises, the Big Wheel (huge heated and air condition
host_about:
I have received four covid vaccines, including the booster, and I will only allow guests into my home who are fully vaccinated. I am retired, and am usually home, so if there is anything you need, I’m always happy to assist. I can also help you navigate the area, and discuss your itinerary with suggestions and ideas, to make the most of your time in Seattle. 

I have been told numerous times from guests that “this is not your normal or ordinary Airbnb,” which I consider to be a compliment. If you are an art appreciator, have an artistic flair, or simply want to engage your senses, you just may enjoy staying here. I have lived in Seattle over 42 years; all of which were in Queen Anne, which is unmistakably the most prestigious, and highly sought after location in Seattle. The former Governor of Washington and the Chinese ambassador lived 2 blocks away, and Sue Bird of the Seattle Storm was 3 houses from me. 

It’s a very quiet neighborhood, filled with charming turn of the century homes, (except for mine which is contemporary) and there are no apartment buildings, or developments, which adds to the serenity of the area. Bigelow Ave is a historical street, lined with huge trees, and a viewpoint one block from me that is a major viewing area for the 4th of July fireworks, and is a primary stop for tour buses. It overlooks Lake Union, which is filled with boats, houseboats, Cascade mountain view’s, and is where the houseboat that was instrumental in the movie “Sleepless in Seattle” was filmed. 

If you stroll down Bigelow Ave, you will find many city views.  I’m located one mile from Seattle Center and two miles from downtown. The bus which takes you directly to both locations, and is one block from my home. The majority of the attractions are very close to my home, so unless you plan day trips, you won’t need a car. I can direct you how to get to my home from the airport by public transportation which is simple; one train and one bus ride, and it’ll be less than $6 per person. 

Queen Anne Avenue is eight blocks away, which has dozens of dining choices, bars, shops, banks, Trader Joe’s, a drug store, and many restaurants offer outdoor dining. In the colder months, the outside secluded personal booths have heaters. 

If you prefer a sparse, refined, buttoned-down, or minimalistic setting, this is not the home for you, and it would be best for you to secure other lodging. This home is the embodiment of a modern, cool, and trendy abode, in combination with a chill and relaxed attitude. 

However, if you want to visit Seattle, and stay at my home; there is virtually nothing that you need to bring, except your clothes, and if you need robes, coats, or jackets, I have plenty of them available. The bedroom and bathroom are filled with absolutely everything that you may need, or not even realize that you may need, and every possible convenience is contained within your space, as well as the coziness and comforts that will contribute to ensuring that you have the best experience possible. 

I am a world traveler and I understand the importance of a quiet, comfortable, cozy, and inviting atmosphere after a day of traveling, driving, flying, touring, sightseeing, visiting with family and friends, and dealing with crowds, traffic, and lines during high tourist season. 
If you are arriving by car, there is always ample free parking on my block; one of the last neighborhoods in Seattle with this luxury. If you need your laundry done, before, during, or when you depart, I will do it for you. 

If you stay at my home, you will be welcomed with gracious hospitality, elegant sheets, goose down and multiple Tempurpedic pillows, a large closet, an aromatherapy diffuser, and a sound machine with many possible water choices; rain, two surf modes, thunderstorm, pond, white noise, and it can also be customized to add the sound of frogs, owls, birds, etc. 

The room is fully inclusive, and you will find, robes, a heated towel warmer, an abundance of emollients for both men and women, a blow dryer, a flat iron, a curling iron, an assortment of hair products, toothpaste, toothbrushes, dental floss, Q-tips, cotton balls, toothpicks, pain relievers, and a private bathrooms stocked with everything you could possibly need. There is a large assortment of body washes, shampoos, conditioners, lotions, and potions. Also, an assortment of skin care products for men. I’ve been told many times by guests after they have arrived home, that now their husbands, partners, boyfriends, or male friends, are hooked, and are now indulging in self care skin and body care products. A weighted blanket and a relaxing foot massager is also available. 

It also has several dimmable steampunk fixtures, a Keurig coffee machine with a huge assortment of coffee. I always make sure the room has snacks, chocolate, candy, a mini fridge, a microwave, and an antique ice chest which is full of dishes, utensils, glasses, wine glasses, a corkscrew, dozens of tea choices, napkins, go cups, and basically anything you may need. The room also has a leather love seat, a desk, and a large Samsung HD TV with Netflix, HBO, Showtime and many other choices. I will welcome you with wine or beer upon your arrival if you choose to indulge. 

The bedroom will pamper you with soothing comforts, a king size Temperpedic bed whcih adjusted for both your bed and your feet, a heated mattress pad to ensure you’ll be toasty when you crawl in bed in the cooler climates, which is dual controlled and has three heating zones, so you can customize where you want heat to be distributed. For the warmer months, the house has a brand new air conditioning system, and a Dyson tower fan for the room. I’ve been told so many times that the space is like a spa, and that I have comforts that the guests didn’t realize even existed. 
I have volunteered at the Seattle Animal Shelter for over 14 years as their official mascot at sporting, fundraising, and adoption events. It's always a thrill giving hugs and high-fives to kids and adults alike, not to mention hundreds of selfies as Fido the bloodhound.

I have two adorable Yorkie puppies, and a 7  year old Lhasa Apso. I also have a 22 year old African Grey parrot, who speaks and mimics, however she is on the main floor, and your space is on the 2nd floor. 

This home is not suited for children; infants, toddlers, as well as school aged kids, due to small pets, and lots of art in the common areas, much of it is breakable, or not to be touched or played with, as well as bed wetting.  There is a flight of stairs up to the house, and another flight inside. Because of previous bad experiences, I only accept adults. There are always exceptions, so please let me know what your situation is, so that I can access if this is a good fit. 

Seattle was the first state in 2014 to legalize both pot and gay marriage, and is extremely liberal.  If you choose to smoke, I simply ask that you do it outside on my porch, or you can walk one block to the amazing viewpoint where there is seating. 

You are welcome to smoke as long as it is outside. There is a porch with tables and chairs, and the viewpoint one block away has a bench where you can enjoy the beautiful view.

Located in West Seattle, about 15 minutes from downtown. A trip to Alki Beach and drive along the water has few, if any, equals in the city. It features stunning views of the downtown skyline and across Puget Sound. It has a sparkling sand beach that imparts a resort character and prompts an undeniable hunger for fish and chips. For those prospective guests who are averse to seeing homeless people or panhandlers, I suggest avoiding downtown Seattle altogether.

South Park was first settled in 1851. It sits on the west bank of the Duwamish River, the only river in the city of Seattle. It was once a small town of Italian and Japanese farmers who supplied fresh produce to Seattle's Pike Place Market and is home to the last working farm (Marra Farm) in the city. In 1920 the Duwamish River was re-channeled into a straight, deep channel that would accept ocean-going ships and barges. host_about:
I am originally from Albuquerque, New Mexico and now a longtime resident of the PNW. I absolutely love living in the PNW with all its natural beauty and opportunity to indulge my passions. Seattle has so much to offer with events and places to explore. However, I am a desert girl at heart and regularly visit the SW for my Rocky Mountain fix. 

My passions include cooking, foraging, hiking, gardening, sailing, and knitting. I love tending my chickens and hiking with my dogs, Meg and Grady. But, most of all, I love meeting new people, getting to know them, and learning about all their adventures. As a former professional Personal and Executive assistant, I very much enjoy taking care of people and their needs. This is why I love being an Airbnb host. Nothing gives me greater pleasure than making a difference in peoples lives. I love cooking delicious meals for my guests and making sure they are comfortable and cozy in their suite. It is my goal as a host for my guests to leave here feeling more enriched by their experience. 

For my own enrichment I listen to a lot of audio books. I don't have much time to sit and read, so I listen while I work. I enjoy almost all genres, but I particularly enjoy historical fiction (Sharon Kay Penman, Edward Rutherford, Herman Wouk, Ken Follett) fantasy (Diana Gabaldon, Orson Scott Card, Jonathan Renshaw, Neil Gaimon, Dean Koontz, Robert McCammon), mystery (John LeCarre, Rhys Bowen, Jacqueline Winspear) and many others. A couple of my favorite books are "East of Eden" by John Steinbeck and "The Good Earth" by Pearl S. Buck. If you haven't read them, DO! 

I love to travel and a bike trip across France or Italy is in my bucket list. I'm not a "fancy" traveler and prefer the simple life. I love to camp and stay in rustic cabins. One of my favorite vacation spots is Iron Springs Resort. It is not rustic, but the cabins are nostalgic and comfortable. I have many good memories there. Another favorite spot is Lake Ozette in the Olympic National Forest. I had the best canoe camping trip there ever. Many of the campsites at Lake Ozette are only accessible by boat. It is a beautiful place and within hiking distance of ocean beaches. I love adventure and live by the motto "Life is an adventure! Live it!!". I hope you will come share some of your own adventures with me.

description: The quiet and cozy Captain’s Cottage is an homage to the unique history of Ballard, where a large population of Scandinavians worked in the boat building industry at the turn of the 20th century. neighborhood_overview:
Ballard is a hip neighborhood with a unique history in Seattle, Washington. At the turn of the 20th century Ballard was its own city, a center for boat and shingle making. Many immigrants from Scandinavian countries set up camp in Ballard and today it is home to the National Nordic Heritage Museum, host to the 2nd largest Settende Mai (17th of May) Norwegian Constitution Day parade in the world and a fantastic Sunday market featuring artisanal products and local delicacies.

With 11 breweries in just 5 square miles, Ballard has become a tourist destination for beer. In fact, Ballard is home to more breweries than any other Seattle or Portland neighborhood.

Nearby attractions include Shilshole Beach, the Locks and Green Lake, great places to bike or walk.

The neighborhood sits on the highest named hill in the city, with a maximum elevation of 456 feet (139 m). It covers an area of 7.3 square kilometers (2.8 sq mi), and has a population of about 28,000. Queen Anne is bordered by Belltown to the south, Lake Union to the east, the Lake Washington Ship Cana and Fremont to the north and Interbay to the west.

name: Architectural Gem, Light-filled, Modern & Cosy
description: TheSteelAway is a detached backyard guesthouse. Experience contemporary design at its finest in our thoughtfully crafted house nestled in a residential neighborhood on the edge of Ballard’s Brewery District, right between two of Seattle’s most vibrant neighborhoods: Ballard & Fremont, you will be close to many of Seattle's top destinations for dining, shopping, & nightlife. Enjoy designer finishes, amazing natural light and a stunning sunset view of the Olympic Mountains when the clouds part.
neighborhood_overview: Within just 5 blocks you will find the Burke Gilman bike & walking trail, the Ross Park playground, two grocery stores, a pharmacy, a coffee shop, a liquor store, a pot shop, burgers, pizza and a handful of breweries.    Ballard & Fremont each have their own Sunday markets, both well worth taking advantage off.  Due to its location between Fremont & Ballard, our microneighborhood is often called Frelard and has been recently developing a new character of its own.  There has been an influx of musicians using the practice spaces that have been built in nearby warehouses and what began as an underground music club offshoot has begun to draw a crowd. Take a short walk around this zone and you may also find the Ice Box Arcade tucked behind the old Allied Ice office, or stumble upon the studio of a well-know local artist that is open to the public on weekends.  The studio where Nirvana recorded their first album is 5 blocks away.  See if you can guess which building it is.
host_about: I love travel and architecture. Staying in great spaces makes such a difference while traveling and I love staying in neighborhoods with a local vibe. I designed The Steel Away guesthouse in Seattle as a great entryway to and respite from all there is to engage with in Ballard, Fremont and greater Seattle.  My condo in San Miguel de Allende is occasionally available for rent when I am away. I adore both of these spaces and hope you will too!

Are you a foodie ???

Our Space
---------------
Our space is hard to describe but we have been compared to a scrappy McMenamin's We have a large space but very clean and magical ( built as a hotel in 1904) our historical building has been lovingly restored .
We are not your usual space so please read carefully... think old school hotel / European hostel without the ghosts....or maybe there are ghosts you will have to see (wink wink) No ghosts that  are too precocious I promise :)
We have three shared and very clean bathrooms
One very well stocked kitchen (pots, pans, dishes and the like provided) 
And if you enjoy a morning coffee or tea / or evening glass of wine (or smoke) we have a very expansive back porch with couches , tables and a designated smoking area (New Orleans meets Georgetown)

 If you are sick please do not travel.  I'm a fairly warm person, i like to give hugs but currently I am keeping social distancing and ask that if you visit us that you do also.  
About Me 
I LOVE LOVE LOVE being a host, traveling and meeting awesome people. I have recently adopted a little girl doggie named Pickles who is sweet and learning how to greet people, she came all the way from Mexico but is not traumatized at all, if you are allergic to dogs then please let me know before hand so i can have her in my office.   
 The building is truly a magical charmer and  I think you will enjoy your stay here

Special things to be aware of
* I follow Airbnb’s enhanced cleaning protocol, which was developed with expert guidance.


***Please note that the rooms are on the second floor and we unfortunately are not ADA accesible. 

***Also of note our space is in the city so it's active and not always cricket quiet some noise from events , street or airplanes may happen, if you need a super quiet space book a hotel in the country. Most of the time the building itself is quiet but we have planes that fly overhead and a hopping building with fun restaurants and a pool hall downstairs. 

HANDS ON / only one staff member / so please be communicative
 I only have one staff member and do all cleaning, booking and greeting (except evening arrivals) myself so it is appreciated that you let me know your arrival time (as close as possible) at the time of your booking request and communicate this when you book if possible. I greet you in person or our evening manager if your arrival is after 6 pm 
***After 10 pm arrivals \late arrivals will require a $20 hr surcharge**. Late arrivals  with prior arrangement may be accepted) please inform me of your arrival time at the time of your booking request. Of course we know that emergencies happen ( delayed flights are real) and will work with you to make sure you are safe and respected

About ME
   I am an artist , entrepreneur and lover of people, plants and four legged beings. Sadly we can not allow animals in the rooms at this time unless they are a documented service animal with a vets authorization (must provide before booking)
   I  easy going person and  always try to keep our space filled with good energy. We welcome all respectful people here, this is a safe space. 
* please be vaccinated so we may keep everyone safe. Currently we are not requiring masking or social distancing in shared spaces , but you may do what ever makes you comfortable and please if you are immunocompromised just let us know and we will also wear our masks for you. Just let us know.

****Please no non Airbnb guests onsite unless they are helping you with your luggage , or help up and down stairs

I  am easily accessible if you need anything, I am happy to oblige most requests and strive to make every traveler feel welcome  but I also will give you your space. I try to take Sundays off to rest and have time with my dog. (Dog lives off site )
I am also happy to  help you plan a fun day here in Seattle.  I have allot of travel info and happy to give you any recommendations . 


We look forward to meeting you and making your stay awesome!

name: Cozy 1 Bedroom Apt Near Children’s Hospital and UW
description:
Enter this newly-renovated apartment through a private entrance off a spacious garden deck on the first floor of our 1926 stucco home, located in the lovely Laurelhurst neighborhood of Northeast Seattle, known for beautiful homes, rolling hills, and scenic pathways.

Our neighborhood is safe, quiet and garden-like, yet only minutes from UW, Children’s Hospital, and Downtown Seattle. University Village, a unique and upscale outdoor mall nearby, offers shopping and wonderful restaurants.
neighborhood_overview:
Our neighborhood is essentially a single-family-home hilly cul-de-sac on top of the Laurelhurst hill, so it’s very private and safe. It is great for walking, with good lighting and sidewalks, beautiful landscaped yards and views of lake and mountains along the way. You will see all different styles of houses, from early 1920’s to Modern, from middle class family homes to waterfront mansions.

There are a lot of excellent dining options in Northeast Seattle and University Village, and there are several parks and outdoor nature areas nearby.

We are just a short walk to the Laurelhurst Park, which has a round 1.2 mile loop trail walk, tennis courts, playground, sports fields, beautiful mature trees and Community Center; Union Bay Nature Area which has several trails with views of Lake Washington and great bird and possibly animal viewing; and the Yesler Swamp with its recently constructed boardwalk to explore a marshy area where birds and beavers live.

Lau
host_about:
We feel truly lucky to call Seattle home!  Our family  owns two Seattle houses dating to 1926 and 1947.  You'll probably see us working around their yards which we tend to do a lot!

Welcome to Maple Leaf neighborhood in my beloved Seattle, also known as the Emerald City.  

My commitment to my guests is to make your stay as relaxing and memorable as possible. 

Everything you could possibly need is within your grasp.  

Walking around the neighborhood is an adventure, so bring some comfortable walking shoes and plan on getting some exercise.  Taking in the many coffee shops, cafes, and boutiques in between you will see that Seattle has adapted to Covid-19 with outdoor seating at most restaurants or Take-Out ordering. If you ever have any questions, I am always a text away with an answer and a smile!

When I am not helping my clients in the apartment, I am helping people find their way in the world of real estate as a full-time Realtor.  It brings me great joy & fulfillment when I support my clients as they search to buy a new dream home or prepare their beloved family home to Sell to a new family. 

Whatever the reason in every season, I am committed to being of service & helping my clients with their real estate needs.

I enjoy meeting people and hearing what makes them tick. I love to travel,  study architecture, art, design, food, fashion, wine, and culture. 

Having a passion for helping find homeless animals their Furever Homes, know that a percentage of your fee is donated to local Animal Shelters & Rescue organizations across the US and internationally; the animals thank you!  

In my spare time, I am seen walking my two rescue pups, Charli & Bolty, in our beautiful Maple Leaf neighborhood, Maple Leaf park, or around Greenlake park! 

Last and certainly not least, I have a passion for volunteering with Habitat 4 Humanity! I love to learn new skills and I enjoy building homes for families in need; helping put a roof over a family's heads is one of the most rewarding experiences I have had and I highly recommend it! 

My philosophy is that life is one big Adventure novel made up of lots of little exciting chapters! 

We live and we learn… 

Everyone needs a home (while on the road) where they feel safe, they can hang their hat, relax & regroup for their next adventure!

Welcome to my home & world filled with rescue animals, flower gardens, and GF muffins/cookies (which I love to bake & deliver outside your front door). 

Thank you for being our guest,
Alex, Charli & Bolty

Then, of course, there’s Alki, the sandy beach strip on the tip of the peninsula.

The neighborhood is pretty quiet. The windows do a pretty good job of blocking out the vehicular traffic on the roads around, allowing you to have a good cozy retreat!

The Mariners and Seahawks stadiums are directly across the water from the house and a 10 minute Uber away.

description:
Welcome to Caravan-Serai Inn and the Wallingford/Fremont neighborhood of Seattle! Just blocks from Lake Union and Gasworks Park, tons of dining options, and easy access to downtown Seattle, you will find everything you need in this newly remodeled apartment. 2 bedrooms, one bath, kitchenette, a spacious dining room and living room with spectacular views of Lake Union, downtown and Mount Rainier.

neighborhood_overview:
Caravan-Serai Inn is located on the edge of the Fremont neighborhood, known for its eclectic flair, restaurants, and kitschy sights to see (has anyone seen a troll around here?). Peruse some vintage clothing shops or a record shop in Fremont, explore the Locks, and enjoy some of the best and freshest seafood in one of the many restaurants nearby.

We are also considered to be on the edge of the Wallingford neighborhood, also home to many fine restaurants and small shops. Woodland Park Zoo is nearby, as well as Green Lake Park and walking trails. Gasworks Park is just northeast of the Inn, and from there you can connect to the Burke Gilman Trail - a paved pathway for cyclists and walkers that stretches from Redmond in the east to Ballard in the west - if you are an avid cycler, you can bike for miles and miles along this path and see the city from a different perspective.
host_about:
I was born in Madaba, Jordan, and immigrated with my family to the United States when I was a very young child. I grew up in Seattle, and hold B.A. and M.A. degrees from the University of Washington. I have lived and traveled extensively throughout the Middle East, North Africa, Iran, and Europe.

The history of the Zawaideh clan is fascinating. My lineage can be traced back to the earliest roots of man in Yemen. My ancestors were among the first settled tribes to migrate from that area, moving northeast to what is now southern Iraq and later to what are now the modern countries of Jordan and Syria. 

You can read more about my family history in our Welcome Book during your stay. I come from a culture of hospitality and exploration, and I hope you will get a taste of that during your stay at the Caravan-Serai Inn.

name: Craftsman Comfort in Capital Hill
description: Welcome to this one bedroom apartment in the centrally-located, north end of Capitol Hill. The bright, remodeled garden level space matches the character of this historic craftsman home built in 1914. The neighborhood is walkable and fun! It is one of the best neighborhoods in Seattle for strolls to take in the nearby early 20th century architecture and lush gardens. The apartment is close to Volunteer Park, Interlaken Park, Copper Tree Coffee, the Broadway restaurant district, and more!
neighborhood_overview:
The Capitol Hill neighborhood is not only a beautiful and safe residential area, but also the top destination for restaurants, nightlife, and entertainment in Seattle. The Broadway restaurant area is a 20 minute walk and the famous Pike/Pine corridor is a 30 minute walk. Both areas can be reached by bus (#49) within less than 10 minutes or by car in 5 to 8 minutes. If you have a car, freeway entrances are close and it is the most central place for getting around Seattle and the east side. You can easily reach downtown on bus #49 in less than 15 minutes. The light rail station is a 25 minute walk from the house. There are often rental bikes nearby as well.

We are close to parks and some delicious restaurants! The best parks include Volunteer Park (with the famous water tower, art museum, conservatory, and view of the Space Needle), Interlaken Park (for a Northwest forest walk within the city), Roanoke Park, the Arboretum (incredible and extensive park with trees and gardens
host_about:
I love the great outdoors, travel, food, and my family! 

As a guest I'm respectful and communicative. 

I was an Airbnb host in the past so I understand caring for your place.

Are you a foodie ???

Our Space

Bobby

host_about: Hi! I'm a parent, author, and hobby farmer living in Seattle's Ballard neighborhood with my family. I'm married to Dan, who works in the travel industry, and we have two awesome kids. Our roots go way back in the Pacific Northwest, but before settling in Seattle for good, we lived as far away as Amsterdam and Australia. We love our friendly, colorful, epicurean, walkable, bikeable, open-hearted neighborhood--and the truly spectacular region we're lucky to call home. Traveling the world with our kids, we've always looked for farm stays, fresh eggs, backyard goats, blooming gardens, and other features that keep us close to the refreshing magic of the natural world. In fact, it was an Airbnb host in Oregon (Sweet Springs Family Farm) who inspired us to add bunnies to our homestead, and an Airbnb host in France (Aux Fenêtres du Château) serving bitty brown speckled eggs at breakfast who kindled our interest in keeping a flock of quail at home in Seattle. We have always enjoyed hosting Airbnb guests over the years in our primary residence (Hummingbird House in Ballard) whenever we've taken off on family adventures. In summer 2021, after 9 precious years with our kids growing up side by side, our beloved next-door neighbors moved away. They sold their beautiful home to us, so we could expand our farm and begin hosting guests full-time. We look forward to welcoming you to Peach Street Farm, Seattle's first urban farmstay, where you can relax and explore at your own pace.

description: MONTHLY RENTAL - Soak in the beauty of the Pacific Northwest at our Seattle beach house that features panoramic views of the water & Olympic mountains. The CD has a number of designated historical landmarks:

- Immaculate Conception Church, 820 18th Avenue (1904)
- - Old Firehouse #23, CAMP, 722 18th Avenue (1909)
- Victorian House, 1414 S. Washington Street (1900)
- Langston Hughes Cultural Arts Center (formerly Bikur Cholim Synagogue) 104 17th Avenue (1912)

- James Washington Jr. Home and Studio, 1816 26th Avenue (1918)
- First African Metho

Born and raised in the Montana, my craze for mountain adventure was ignited by the awe-inspiring Rocky Mountains and led me to Seattle 30 years ago where I have climbed, scaled, scrambled, skied, criss-crossed, trudged, trekked, hiked, biked and kayaked some of the Pacific Northwest’s classic adventures and hidden gems.  

My impetus to see the world began with an obsession to climb in some of the world’s highest mountains. Eventually, a climate of moralism against "boozers from Seattle" invading the area and a series of political scandals contributed to Luna Park's demise, and it closed forever in 1913.

name: Chic Wallingford townhome
description: Feel instantly at home in this stylish townhouse in Wallingford. 2 bedrooms, 2.5 baths, and a thoughtfully equipped work-ready office with everything you need to stay productive. Fast internet, vintage audio, elegant antique glassware, and a well-appointed kitchen that makes cooking an event (in a good way!). Best of all, you'll be in one of the most coveted locations in the city. Walk to many of Seattle's best restaurants; 10 min drive to downtown or UW; 5 mins to Green Lake or the zoo.
neighborhood_overview: Wallingford is the best neighborhood in Seattle. It's just true! Close to downtown, UW, the zoo, and an easy straight shot to all things north; just a bit farther to Ballard, the locks, Golden Gardens beach, Magnolia. The townhome is just a few blocks from beautiful Woodland Park and Green Lake if you like to walk or take your dogs for a romp. You are 2 blocks from a long stretch of walkable fun on 45th packed with restaurants, bars, shopping, and quirky fun things to discover. Turn right down Stone Way toward the Lake Union marinas and find Seawolf Bakery, Fiasco, The Whale Wins, and all the incredible eateries Fremont has to offer. It's neighborhood that welcomes families, singles, retirees, and all types of people. Very walkable, quite safe, and charming as can be. Venture out and you're going to love it.
host_about: I first moved to Seattle in 1999 to hop on board the tech wave and I've enjoyed the city and surrounding area from almost every neighborhood—but Wallingford is by far my favorite. In recent years I've been traveling more than not, enjoying other people's beautiful spaces all over the world, and opening mine up when I'm gone.

We are located in the one of the core Seattle neighborhoods (Capitol Hill), on the border of Madison Park.

When traveling, we're on the look out for the tastiest food spots, live music, best views, and any sort of fun, cultural events unique to that place. We hope to venture to many new places together. We look forward to hosting you!

Cheers,
Laura and Josh

neighborhood_overview:
Queen Anne is one of the most iconic neighborhoods in Seattle for good reason! It is home to the Space Needle, runs along the beautiful shore of Lake Union, and is home to some of Seattle’s most beautiful historic homes and timeless architecture. In Queen Anne, you’ll soak in the most memorable views of the city — the glistening waters of Puget Sound and the rugged peaks of the Olympic Range and Mount Rainier are some of the most notable highlights. Take a walk over to Kerry Park (AKA, the Queen Anne Hill) for some of the best cliffside viewing of the rugged Pacific Northwest and a stroll around manicured gardens and lush landscapes.

Queen Anne also offers more urban sightseeing than any visitor could fit into a day! In 2018 I started my company, HOST JEEVES, to manage investment/vacation properties for other owners. It’s been great so far.

As your host, I will do everything to ensure you have an amazing experience. Please come and be my guest for a truly memorable stay!
